clue.text: In charge in class, he has a worn-out expression

indicators.note: the second 'in' tells us to place one piece inside the letters that follow it

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
taken as written
officers' shorthand abbreviates this phrase to IC

explanation.surface: A teacher in charge of a class keeps repeating a tired phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in charge' as a teacher's job; it is just the abbreviation, slotted into the class abbreviation before HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed phrase that has lost its force through overuse is a stock, stale saying.

clue.text: Inversion of word order as much is rewritten

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents set down afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar note: rewriting a sentence like 'as much is' turns its word order round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges the eight letters of AS MUCH IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhetorical figure in which terms are repeated in reverse order (ABBA pattern) is the classic inversion device.

clue.text: Has a policy for hedges

definitions.meaning: holds an insurance policy covering something
protects oneself against loss, as a hedge in finance does

explanation.surface: A gardener's insurance covers the hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out cover against a risk is both holding a policy and guarding against loss.

clue.text: Cough with pain, having to trim the border

parts.note: a hem is a small throat-clearing cough, as in 'hem and haw'
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: Someone coughing and aching while sewing an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: This decorative needlework, drawing threads together, is used to finish and edge cloth.

clue.text: Inferior position for a motoring adviser

definitions.meaning: a '... driver' is a passenger who gives the driver unwanted advice

explanation.surface: The passenger who tells you how to drive sits in a lowly spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a minor role is 'taking a back seat', and the unwelcome driving critic is the backseat driver.

clue.text: The ensign he sails under is still red, we hear

definitions.text: The ensign he sails under is still red, we hear

parts.words: The ensign he sails under is still red, we hear
parts.note: 'ancient' is an old word for an ensign; a merchant seaman sails under the Red Ensign; and Coleridge's poem about an old sailor is still read, which sounds like 'red'

explanation.surface: A sailor's flag is still red, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Three layers: 'ancient' meant ensign (Iago is Othello's 'ancient'); the Red Ensign is the British merchant navy flag; and 'red' sounds like 'read', since Coleridge's poem is still widely read.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of Coleridge's famous poem, an aged seaman, is still read today.

clue.text: One of the three bears, said the Irishman

definitions.text: One of the three bears, said the Irishman

parts.words: One of the three bears, said the Irishman
parts.note: in a stage Irish accent 'three' comes out as 'tree', so this is one of the tree bears, an Australian marsupial living in eucalyptus trees

explanation.surface: An Irishman retells Goldilocks and names one of the bears.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goldilocks story is a false trail; the joke is the accent turning 'three bears' into 'tree bears'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian marsupial, popularly called a bear, lives in eucalyptus trees.

clue.text: An escape for the number I rescue when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
to rescue is to save

explanation.surface: A convict numbered I escapes by climbing a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns NO + I + SAVE into EVAS I ON, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging or getting away from something is a form of avoidance or getaway.

clue.text: Paid up and went inside, one after another

indicators.note: the word and goes into the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid

explanation.surface: Someone paid at the door and went into the venue, queueing in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Paying a bill is meeting it, a sense solvers often miss; 'up' turns the word in this down clue, and 'went inside' places the joining word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in single file, one behind the other, as on a bicycle built for two.

clue.text: Daisy's on time, Hilary's next

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: the Michaelmas daisy is an autumn aster
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A garden note: the daisy blooms on time, and Hilary's comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy and Hilary look like two people; Hilary is the Oxford spring term, which comes next after the autumn one.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and some other universities the autumn session is followed by the Hilary session, so Hilary's is next after it.

clue.text: What Homer presumably was, apart from occasional lapses

definitions.text: What Homer presumably was, apart from occasional lapses

parts.words: What Homer presumably was, apart from occasional lapses
parts.note: the proverb 'even Homer nods' means the great poet sometimes dozed; apart from those lapses he must have been unable to sleep

explanation.surface: A literary aside on the poet's habitual wakefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer nods' is the proverb for a great writer's occasional slip; read literally, nodding off means he otherwise never slept.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually cannot sleep is a chronic wakeful sufferer.

clue.text: A chief with great strength

parts.note: main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A leader of great might.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning vigorously, at full force.

clue.text: Extend prison sentence

definitions.meaning: slang for a term in jail

explanation.surface: Lengthening someone's time inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out is to lengthen, and a spell in jail is slang for a term inside.

clue.text: Question vet

explanation.surface: Interrogate the animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate and to scrutinise both mean to look closely into something.

clue.text: Raised group turnover

parts.note: up means raised, as in 'hands up'
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A team's financial turnover has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Overturning something, or an unexpected reversal of result, is a turnover.

clue.text: Put on a pedestal, then Reno split up

indicators.note: a couple splitting up in Reno, the divorce capital, scatters these letters

explanation.surface: A couple put each other on a pedestal, then divorced in Reno.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces, which makes 'split up' a natural anagram cue here.
explanation.definitionFit: To place on a throne is to exalt, raising someone to a revered position.

clue.text: Restorer is in Verona to repair head of Raphael

indicators.note: repair is read as an anagram cue, with to joining it: the town's letters get fixed into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A restorer works in Verona on a painting of Raphael's.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures restoring a painting; 'is in' is just a link, and the art-restorer image hides an anagram of the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who renovates brings a building or object back to good condition.

clue.text: Ken Smith is wrong in my opinion

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: In my view Ken Smith is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic way of saying 'it seems to me', introducing a personal view.

clue.text: Inoffensive word sergeant-major exchanged with a girl

indicators.note: one piece is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: a euphemism is a mild word used in place of an offensive one

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major softens his language when talking with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged with' swaps the final SM of the mild-word term for A.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: A French composer for you to solve

parts.note: un is French for a
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter offers a French composer for you to work out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpick a tangle or a mystery is to work it out.

clue.text: Directions about a pair of spectacles worn round the neck

indicators.note: the directions go round the other piece

parts.note: N, S and E are compass directions north, south and east
OO looks like a pair of round lenses

explanation.surface: Glasses on a cord worn around the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures glasses on a neck-cord, but the thing worn round the neck is a hangman's loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's loop of rope is placed around the throat.

clue.text: Skill needed for reading on crowded Japanese trains?

definitions.text: Skill needed for reading on crowded Japanese trains?

parts.words: Skill needed for reading on crowded Japanese trains?
parts.note: on a packed commuter train a newspaper must be folded very small to be read, so the Japanese art of paper folding would help

explanation.surface: Commuters in Tokyo need a knack to read papers in the crush.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading suggests literacy, but the skill is folding the paper small.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Bid raised to impress

parts.note: a call is a bid in bridge
up means raised

explanation.surface: An auction bid is raised to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to force into military service, as conscription summons people to serve.

clue.text: Fitting in a proposed date

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a suggested date for a dress fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like a tailor's appointment; it is the definition, meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent or opportune is to the point and appropriate.

clue.text: St Bernard running wild in India?

definitions.text: St Bernard running wild in India?

parts.words: St Bernard running wild in India?
parts.note: a St Bernard is a kind of dog; a dog running wild in India is the ownerless stray of the subcontinent

explanation.surface: A rescue dog loose on the streets of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Bernard stands for any dog; the question mark flags that a stray in India is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-wild, ownerless mongrel of India and Asia is a stray dog.

clue.text: Rail is the fashionable way, said Sam Weller

indicators.note: Sam Weller in Dickens's Pickwick Papers swaps his v and w sounds, so a w comes out as v

parts.note: in means fashionable, followed by way

explanation.surface: A Dickensian character recommends rail travel as the stylish way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said Sam Weller': Weller, Mr Pickwick's servant, says 'vay' for 'way', so IN WAY becomes the word for protest. 'Rail' looks like trains.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily, to rant against something.

clue.text: Girl in hat of bluish colour

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A girl in a blue hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally names the bluish-grey colour of bruised skin.

clue.text: Irritation from detached retina? Yes

indicators.note: a detached retina breaks loose, so these letters come apart and reform

explanation.surface: An eye patient's discomfort from a detached retina, confirmed by the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and soreness of the eyes from overuse is a kind of ocular irritation.

clue.text: She sounds high — from over-matiness?

indicators.note: the pieces are spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name, standing for 'she'
game that is high is gamy, slightly off

explanation.surface: A woman sounding off loftily about too much familiarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' applies to the girl's name, giving its first part; over-matiness puns on having too many mates, that is spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Having several spouses at once means too much marrying, a pun on mates as partners.

clue.text: Tracks for dogs

definitions.meaning: follows closely, as a dog does

explanation.surface: Paths for hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Footpaths or marks left behind, and to follow someone persistently, as a pursuer does.
